name: Main_Table_1
title: Table 1. Characteristics of the primary arterial waveform cohort
notes: Values are median [interquartile range] or n (% among valid nonmissing cases). ASA Physical Status was missing in 54 cases; percentages use 2381 cases with valid values. Four included non-donor operations carried source-recorded ASA=6 values incompatible with the operative context; because no audit trail was available for adjudication, these values were treated as missing. No ASA V cases were recorded. ASA, American Society of Anesthesiologists; NIBP, noninvasive blood pressure.

name: Main_Table_2
title: Table 2. Event visibility and cumulative hypotension exposure by sampling interval
values: Reference events with low display, expected n
notes: MAP threshold: 65 mmHg. All 2435 cases and 2380 subjects are included. The reference row uses observed arterial pressure and represents all 9187 qualifying reference events. Intermittent rows are averages across all 10 s sampling phases; fractional event counts are expected counts, not additional independent events. An event lasts ≥60 s and has low display if any held value is below threshold, including an inherited value. Duration and AUC cover all below-threshold bins, including runs <60 s, not only qualifying events. Pooled TWA is total deficit AUC / 532 190.5 min of valid reference observation, using the same denominator throughout. Initial unavailable display contributes no displayed burden and is not normal pressure. CI resamples subjects (1000 replicates). Detailed uncertainty is in Table S26; directional decomposition remains in Table S6. AUC, area under the deficit curve; CI, confidence interval; MAP, mean arterial pressure; TWA, time-weighted average.

name: Main_Table_3
title: Table 3. Episode visibility and timing with a 5 min display
values: First low display ≥1 min before recovery, %
First low display ≥2 min before recovery, %
Reference AUC before first low display, %
notes: Reference episodes lasted ≥60 s. Values are estimates (95% subject-bootstrap confidence interval; 1000 replicates), averaged across every 10 s phase. Opportunity denominators include all phase-episode pairs; misses contribute their entire reference area to pre-display area. Timing means condition on represented pairs. AUC, area under the deficit curve; MAP, mean arterial pressure.

name: Main_Table_4
title: Table 4. Display information at recorded low-reference infusion adjustments
notes: Low reference denotes MAP below 65 mmHg. Display states use 236 low-reference events in 85 cases from 83 subjects and sum to 100% before rounding. They describe the adjustment instant, not detection at any time during the whole episode reported in Table 3. Recovery persistence is the mean of event-level phase averages in 184 recovery events from 78 subjects. It is restricted to the remainder of the 5 min post-adjustment window and terminates at normal display, missing reference or recurrent hypotension. CIs use subject-cluster resampling. A normal emulated display was not what the treating team necessarily saw. CI, confidence interval; MAP, mean arterial pressure.

name: Supp_Table_S16
title: Supplementary Table S16
notes: Binary-variable means are proportions. AKI, acute kidney injury; ASA, American Society of Anesthesiologists; AUC, area under the deficit curve; SD, standard deviation; SMD, standardised mean difference. Reference AUC per anaesthesia-hour is expressed in mmHg min h-1.

name: Supp_Table_S17
title: Supplementary Table S17
notes: Absolute hidden burden was scaled per 10 mmHg min h-1. Primary adjusted models treated four context-incompatible source-recorded ASA=6 values as missing. The final model additionally used a three-degree-of-freedom spline of log(1 + total reference AUC per anaesthesia-hour). Modified Poisson models used subject-cluster robust variance. Analysis-plan-defined stability criteria required convergence, finite positive confidence limits, at least five events per parameter, and a CI width ratio no greater than 10. VitalDB does not distinguish planned from unplanned ICU admission; this is a supplementary resource-use association. ASA, American Society of Anesthesiologists; AUC, area under the deficit curve; CI, confidence interval; ICU, intensive care unit; RR, relative risk. All three models met these numerical stability criteria.

ASA, American Society of Anesthesiologists.

name: Supp_Table_S23
title: Supplementary Table S23
notes: Mean arterial pressure threshold: 65 mmHg. Each case contributes one average across 30 sampling phases. Area ratios require positive reference deficit area; 42 zero-area cases remain in absolute state-discordance summaries. State discordance excludes display-unavailable time. Case summaries are not pooled exposure ratios. Among 1899 cases with ≥60 s episodes, the miss fraction was 36.7% [24.8 to 50.2%], with 5th to 95th percentiles 3.3 to 70.0%; within-case phase range was 66.7 [50.0 to 100.0] percentage points. Aggregate quantiles are in the workbook; case-level trajectories are not redistributed.

Inherited low display present at onset (overlapping)
notes: Denominator: 9187 reference episodes × 30 phases = 275 610 phase-episode pairs, in 1899 cases. Threshold: mean arterial pressure below 65 mmHg; contiguous low duration ≥60 s. The onset carry-in row overlaps with fresh sampling and must not be added to the first three rows. name: Supp_Table_S25
